findings.problem: §7.3 maps the sales/requests page load to txnAPI.mine({ approvalStatus: 'pending' }), but reading sales/requests/page.tsx shows the page loads ALL confirmed_transactions (all statuses) sorted by date and renders them to the sales user. A pending-only query hides approved and rejected transactions from the user's request history — a visible regression. The page also has a deleteTransaction action that writes back to localStorage (localStorage.setItem('confirmed_transactions', ...)) which §7.3 omits entirely.
findings.fix: Replace §7.3: load via txnAPI.mine() (no status filter) to return all the caller's transactions; deleteTransaction -> txnAPI.remove(id) (owner can remove their own pending; disable delete for approved/rejected or handle 403). Replace the 'transactionApproved' window listener with a re-fetch after each mutation. Explicitly remove the localStorage.setItem write in deleteTransaction.

findings.problem: admin/page.tsx lines 491-498 split approved transactions into a 'paid' bucket (t.status === 'Paid' || t.paymentStatus === 'completed') and a 'not paid' bucket. The design's Transaction schema constrains status to ['Approved','Pending','Rejected'] and defines no paymentStatus field, so the 'paid' bucket will always be empty and the 'not paid' bucket will contain every approved transaction. The dashboard Paid/NotPaid card silently stops working. §7.5 claims the existing approval logic 'works unchanged' which is true for revenue/orders but false for this split.
findings.fix: Either (a) add a paymentStatus: 'paid'|'unpaid' field to the Transaction schema (§3.1) so the Paid/NotPaid filter remains meaningful, or (b) explicitly state the Paid/NotPaid block is dead legacy code (referencing a 'status: Paid' value never set by the sales pages) and must be removed, replacing the dashboard card with a single 'approved' count. Pick one and document it.

findings.problem: sales/payment-requests/page.tsx loads payment_requests and renders them with filter buttons for all/pending/approved/rejected statuses. §7.11 maps the load to txnAPI.mine({ approvalStatus: 'pending' }), which returns only pending requests and makes the approved/rejected filter buttons always show empty lists — a visible regression for the sales user.
findings.fix: Change §7.11 to txnAPI.mine({ source: 'warehouse' }) (no status filter, warehouse source), load all, then client-side filter by req.approvalStatus matching the existing UI filter state. The page's local filter state drives the visible list; the API provides the full dataset.

findings.problem: sales/requests/page.tsx has a delete action. Migrated, this maps to DELETE /api/txn/:id, but §4.1 marks DELETE as admin-only (@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, RoleGuardClass) + @Roles('admin')). §7.3 instructs using txnAPI.remove(id) from a sales page, which will always return 403 for a sales user. Direct contradiction between §4.1 and §7.3.
findings.fix: Decide and document: either (a) keep DELETE admin-only and change §7.3 to call txnAPI.update for cancel (explain that delete is admin-only in §7.3), or (b) change DELETE to allow owner deletion of pending transactions only (service-layer check: if doc.approvalStatus !== 'pending' throw 403; if doc.userId !== userId && !isAdmin throw 403) and update the §4.1 table accordingly.

findings.problem: §5 instructs making TypeOrmModule.forFeature([User, Role]) unconditional in app.module.ts. But auth.module.ts and users.module.ts already register User and Role entities via their own TypeOrmModule.forFeature([User, Role, ...]) calls. Adding a duplicate forFeature in app.module.ts can trigger duplicate-entity registration warnings/errors depending on TypeORM version. The unconditional TypeOrmModule.forRoot(getPostgresConfig()) is what actually fixes the F3 defect; the module-level forFeature calls already depend on the default (unnamed) connection.
findings.fix: In §5, remove the instruction to add TypeOrmModule.forFeature([User, Role]) to app.module.ts. Instead state that the unconditional TypeOrmModule.forRoot(getPostgresConfig()) registered as the default (unnamed) connection is sufficient for all existing module-level TypeOrmModule.forFeature([...]) calls in AuthModule, UsersModule, etc. to resolve. Do not name the TypeORM connection.

findings.problem: main.ts registers ValidationPipe with whitelist: true AND forbidNonWhitelisted: false. The design text in §8 and the F8 resolution implies unknown/extra properties cause a 400 error. With forbidNonWhitelisted: false, extra unknown properties are silently stripped (HTTP 200 returned, extra field absent), not a 400. The security invariant for UpdateTransactionDto (status stripped from owner PATCH) still holds, but the design overstates the error response.
findings.fix: Correct §8: 'With whitelist: true and forbidNonWhitelisted: false, extra properties are silently stripped (HTTP 200 with the extra field absent). No 400 is returned for unknown extra fields. 400 is only returned when a required field is missing or a present field fails its type/enum constraint.' Remove any language implying unknown extra properties cause a 400.

findings.problem: deleteTransaction filters local state then writes localStorage.setItem('confirmed_transactions', JSON.stringify(updated)). If only the load path is addressed, this write-back remains and reintroduces a business-data localStorage key.
findings.fix: Add to §7.3: 'Remove the localStorage.setItem(confirmed_transactions, ...) write in deleteTransaction; the delete is replaced by txnAPI.remove(id) and local state is updated from the API response.'

findings.problem: §7.3 lists both txnAPI.mine({ approvalStatus: 'pending' }) and txnAPI.mine({ status: 'pending' }) in the same paragraph — two different param objects. The page uses approvalStatus for filtering; the capital status field is a different value.
findings.fix: Use txnAPI.mine({ approvalStatus: 'pending' }) consistently (or per F1, txnAPI.mine() with no filter) and remove the duplicate txnAPI.mine({ status: 'pending' }) reference.

findings.location: §7.5 admin/page.tsx Paid/NotPaid block inside legacy API fallback
findings.problem: Lines 491-498 using status === 'Paid' / paymentStatus sit inside the TypeORM legacy API fallback block. The design's instruction to 'remove the API fallback block' would delete this code as a side effect, but §7.5 doesn't acknowledge that the Paid/NotPaid feature is being dropped, which may confuse the implementer.
findings.fix: Add a sentence to §7.5: 'The API fallback block (~lines 373-497) is removed entirely. The Paid/NotPaid split (lines 491-498) within that block referenced a legacy status: Paid value never set by the sales pages and is intentionally not ported.' (Or, if Paid/NotPaid should be preserved, see F2.)
